comment: The separation of adoption, adaptation, and mapping is very useful. But quantifying adoption "coverage" as the proportion of reference elements realized turns an adaptive reference architecture into a completeness checklist. It penalizes context-appropriate omission and may create incentives to buy components that do not solve a priority health problem. Architectural coverage is an input, not an outcome or a sufficient indicator of maturity.

public.text: The separation of adoption, adaptation, and mapping is very useful. But quantifying adoption "coverage" as the proportion of reference elements realized turns an adaptive reference architecture into a completeness checklist. It penalizes context-appropriate omission and may create incentives to buy components that do not solve a priority health problem. Architectural coverage is an input, not an outcome or a sufficient indicator of maturity.
public.suggestedRevision: Less emphasis on component-coverage scoring, with more on goal- and capability-based fitness. Allow justified ‘not applicable/not yet’ decisions. Countries should also assess whether priority use cases work safely and equitably, whether data are used for action, and whether the architecture can evolve sustainably; report component coverage only as descriptive context.
